description: Automated supervised and unsupervised learning: classification, regression, clustering, dimension reduction, feature extraction, anomaly detection, distribution learning and nearest-neighbour search. These functions handle preprocessing and model selection automatically while still allowing explicit method choice.

tools.name: Classify
tools.description: Trains a classifier from labelled examples and returns a ClassifierFunction that predicts classes for new inputs. It selects the algorithm, preprocesses features and tunes hyperparameters automatically. Inputs may be numbers, text, images, audio or mixed associations.
tools.usage:
Classify[{in1 -> out1, in2 -> out2, ...}]
Classify[trainingset, input]
Classify[data, Method -> "RandomForest"]

parameters.name: ValidationSet
parameters.description: Explicit held-out data for model selection.

tools.notes: Ask for "Probabilities" or "TopProbabilities" as a second argument to get confidence instead of a hard label.

tools.name: Predict
tools.description: Trains a regression model from examples with numeric outputs and returns a PredictorFunction. Like Classify it handles preprocessing and method selection automatically. Use it for any supervised task with a continuous target.
tools.usage:
Predict[{in1 -> out1, ...}]
Predict[data, input]
Predict[data, Method -> "GradientBoostedTrees"]
tools.notes: Request "Distribution" from the PredictorFunction to get a predictive distribution rather than a point estimate.

tools.name: ClassifierMeasurements
tools.description: Evaluates a trained classifier on test data, giving accuracy, confusion matrices, ROC curves, precision, recall and many other metrics. Requesting a list of properties returns several at once. It is the standard evaluation step after Classify.

tools.name: PredictorMeasurements
tools.description: Evaluates a trained predictor on test data, reporting error metrics such as RMS error, R-squared, residual plots and comparison plots. It mirrors ClassifierMeasurements for regression. Use it to compare candidate models fairly.

tools.name: Information
tools.description: Returns metadata about an object, including trained ClassifierFunction, PredictorFunction, NetChain, Graph and Entity objects. For machine-learning models it reports the chosen method, training time, feature types and accuracy estimates. It replaces the older ClassifierInformation and PredictorInformation functions.

tools.name: FeatureExtraction
tools.description: Learns a feature-extraction pipeline from example data and returns a reusable FeatureExtractorFunction. The same transformation can then be applied consistently to training and new data. Use it to standardize preprocessing across models.

tools.name: FeatureExtract
tools.description: Extracts numeric feature vectors from data in one step, choosing an appropriate representation for text, images, audio or mixed records. It is the convenience form of FeatureExtraction that returns the features directly. Use it to convert raw objects into vectors for clustering or custom models.

tools.name: DimensionReduction
tools.description: Learns a dimensionality-reduction mapping from data and returns a DimensionReducerFunction that can be applied to new points. Methods include PCA, t-SNE, UMAP-style manifold learning and autoencoders. Use it when you need a reusable projection rather than a one-off embedding.

tools.name: DimensionReduce
tools.description: Reduces the dimensionality of a dataset directly, returning the embedded points. It is the one-shot counterpart of DimensionReduction. Use it for visualization of high-dimensional data in two or three dimensions.
tools.usage:
DimensionReduce[data]
DimensionReduce[data, n]
DimensionReduce[data, n, Method -> "TSNE"]

tools.name: FeatureSpacePlot
tools.description: Embeds data into two dimensions and plots each item at its embedded position, showing images or labels directly. It gives an immediate visual sense of how a dataset clusters. Works with images, text, audio and numeric vectors.

tools.name: FindClusters
tools.description: Partitions data into clusters of similar elements, choosing the number of clusters automatically unless told otherwise. It supports many algorithms and distance functions and works on numbers, vectors, strings, images and more. Use it for unsupervised grouping.
tools.usage:
FindClusters[data]
FindClusters[data, n]
FindClusters[data, Method -> "KMeans", DistanceFunction -> f]

parameters.name: CriterionFunction
parameters.description: How the automatic number of clusters is chosen.

tools.notes: ClusteringComponents returns integer labels instead of grouped data, which is easier to join back onto records.

tools.name: ClusterClassify
tools.description: Clusters data and returns a ClassifierFunction that assigns new points to the discovered clusters. This bridges unsupervised discovery and supervised deployment. Use it when new data must be assigned to existing clusters later.

tools.name: ClusteringTree
tools.description: Builds a hierarchical clustering tree from data, returned as a weighted Graph whose structure reflects merge distances. It exposes the whole hierarchy rather than a single partition. Use it to explore structure at multiple granularities.

tools.name: Dendrogram
tools.description: Draws a dendrogram of a hierarchical clustering, showing merge order and distances. Leaves can display the original data such as images or labels. Use it to choose a cut level and to present clustering results.

tools.name: Nearest
tools.description: Finds the elements of a list nearest to a given point, or builds a reusable NearestFunction for repeated queries. It supports arbitrary distance functions and value/label pairs. Use it for lookup tables, k-NN classification and matching.
tools.usage:
Nearest[list, x]
Nearest[list, x, n]
Nearest[list -> labels, x]
tools.notes: Building a NearestFunction once with Nearest[list] is much faster than repeated Nearest[list, x] calls.

tools.name: NearestNeighborGraph
tools.description: Builds a graph connecting each data point to its nearest neighbours. The resulting Graph supports all network analysis functions, which makes it a bridge between data and graph algorithms. Use it for manifold learning, clustering and outlier detection.

tools.name: FeatureNearest
tools.description: Finds nearest neighbours in a learned feature space rather than in raw coordinates, so images, text and audio can be compared semantically. It returns a NearestFunction over extracted features. Use it for similarity search over unstructured data.

tools.name: AnomalyDetection
tools.description: Learns what normal data looks like and returns an AnomalyDetectorFunction that flags unusual new examples. It is trained on examples of normal behaviour only. Use it for fault detection, fraud screening and data quality control.

tools.name: FindAnomalies
tools.description: Returns the elements of a dataset that look anomalous relative to the rest, in a single call. It is the direct counterpart of AnomalyDetection when no reusable detector is needed. A threshold controls sensitivity.
tools.notes: DeleteAnomalies removes them instead of returning them.

tools.name: DeleteAnomalies
tools.description: Removes anomalous elements from a dataset, returning the cleaned data. It is convenient as a preprocessing step before fitting a model. The same threshold option as FindAnomalies controls strictness.

tools.name: LearnDistribution
tools.description: Learns a generative probability distribution from examples, returning a LearnedDistribution that supports RandomVariate, PDF and conditioning. It handles numeric, categorical, text and image data. Use it for synthetic data generation, imputation and density estimation.

tools.name: SynthesizeMissingValues
tools.description: Fills in Missing entries in a dataset by sampling from a learned joint distribution of the data. Unlike simple mean imputation it preserves correlations between fields. Use it to complete records before analysis or modelling.

tools.name: SequencePredict
tools.description: Learns a model of sequences and returns a SequencePredictorFunction that predicts continuations. It works on lists of tokens, characters or words. Use it for autocomplete, text generation and discrete time-series forecasting.

tools.name: ActiveClassification
tools.description: Builds a classifier while actively choosing which inputs to label next, querying a supplied oracle function. This reduces the number of labels needed to reach a given accuracy. Use it when labelling is expensive, such as experiments or human annotation.
tools.notes: ActivePrediction is the regression analogue; both accept a MaxIterations budget.

tools.name: ActivePrediction
tools.description: Builds a regression model while actively selecting the most informative inputs to sample from an expensive function. It is effectively automated design of experiments and surrogate modelling. Use it to model costly simulations with few evaluations.

tools.name: ClassifierFunction
tools.description: Represents a trained classifier produced by Classify or related functions. Applying it to an input gives a class, and a second argument requests probabilities, decision values or top candidates. It can be saved to a file and reloaded.

tools.name: PredictorFunction
tools.description: Represents a trained regression model produced by Predict. Applying it gives a point prediction, while property requests give the predictive distribution, standard deviation or confidence intervals. Store it with Export to reuse without retraining.

tools.name: TrainImageContentDetector
tools.description: Trains an object detector from images annotated with bounding boxes and class labels. The resulting detector locates and classifies objects in new images. Use it when built-in detection categories do not cover your domain.
tools.notes: Training requires many annotated examples and is computationally heavy; a GPU is strongly recommended.

tools.name: TrainTextContentDetector
tools.description: Trains a model that finds and classifies spans of interest inside text, such as custom named entities. Training data pairs text with labelled substrings. Use it for domain-specific information extraction.
